# A GTK window class written as a node is a toplevel inside a container, which
# GTK refuses at run time -- and its constructor wants the application, which
# no container has. A window is what ui.window is, and the runtime makes the
# window there; a class made with another object is declared neither by the
# platform nor by the gir: package (declgen's ctorTakesPointer), so naming one
# is an unknown component, not a program handing GTK a null application.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --opt gir=builtin --out out app.sngl
stderr 'unknown component "gtk.GtkApplicationWindow"'

-- app.sngl --
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"
import ui "sngl:ui"

ui.window(title="Outer") {
    gtk.GtkApplicationWindow(title="Inner") {
        gtk.GtkLabel(label="hello") {}
    }
}
